articles.title: Repressed! Trump bans CNN, MSNow, Politico from Oval Office
articles.summary: US News: The TOI correspondent from Washington: MAGA boss Donald Trump has the sort of relationship with the US media that therapists may describe as “complica.
articles.body: The TOI correspondent from Washington: MAGA boss Donald Trump has the sort of relationship with the US media that therapists may describe as “complicated”: he can't live with them, can’t live without them, can't stop talking about them, and gets mad whenever they say something unflattering.On Friday, he tried the presidential equivalent of blocking their number, announcing a ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House after accusing them of peddling “FAKE NEWS” and failing to give him the sort of coverage he believes he deserves. Other outlets, he warned, could soon join the White House blacklist.It was, in classic Trump fashion, a declaration made first on Truth Social and explained later in a ramble at the White House. “You get so tired of reading and seeing fake news,” he told reporters, complaining that the three organizations “purposely write negative news,” and the decision was “cumulative” rather than prompted by one particular story.Trump and the White House press corps have been here before. In 2018, the White House revoked then CNN correspondent Jim Acosta's hard pass after a contentious exchange with Trump during a news conference. CNN sued, and a federal judge ordered Acosta's credentials temporarily restored, citing due-process concerns, and the White House ultimately restored them permanently. Acosta, now watching the sequel from outside the White House as a podcaster, offered an understated assessment of the latest ban: “I have a feeling this is not going to work out the way he thinks it will.”Trump, naturally, has a different outcome in mind. Asked why this time should be different, he essentially replied: we'll see -- and suggested that the result could depend on which judge hears the case, boasting, at one point, “I got more bans going than any human being.” He also indicated that the ban would apply only to the Oval Office to get around any legal and constitutional wrinkle.Legally, the White House is not obliged to turn the Oval Office into a public-access newsroom. The principle dates to Sherrill v. Knight, the 1977 D.C. Circuit case involving a journalist denied a White House press pass. The court held that while the government need not open the White House to the press, once it establishes press facilities for bona fide journalists, access cannot be denied arbitrarily or because of the journalist's reporting. It also required notice, an opportunity to rebut the reasons for denial and a written decision.More recently though, the DC Circuit court has described the White House press area as a nonpublic forum, which gives the administration substantial discretion over access, but restrictions must still be reasonable and viewpoint-neutral. In other words: the president can control access; but he cannot necessarily control access by deciding who writes nice things about him -- something Trump transparently desires.((White House Correspondents' Association President Jacqui Heinrich put it more formally: “The Constitution protects the freedom of the press from government interference. That protection does not depend on whether the president likes a news organization’s coverage, agrees with its reporting, or approves of the questions its journalists ask.” Seth Stern at the Freedom of the Press Foundation put it more bluntly, saying it is “hard to imagine a dumber move.” ))There is a peculiar paradox at the heart of Trump's relationship with journalists. He is arguably the most voluble and media-saturated president in U.S history, calling reporters into the Oval Office frequently, conducting impromptu interviews, staging gaggles aboard Air Force One, and posting constantly on social media. TV cameras are his oxygen.Yet he has repeatedly demonstrated that what he wants from the press is not necessarily independence but flattery. Negative coverage becomes “fake news,” tough questions – particularly from female reporters – become “nasty,” and critical media has been characterized as the “enemy of the people.”Last November, when Bloomberg correspondent Catherine Lucey asked Trump about Jeffrey Epstein's emails aboard Air Force One, he pointed at her and said: “Quiet, piggy!” The White House defended his language as evidence of his supposedly frank relationship with reporters. He has also called female reporters “obnoxious,” made gratuitous personal comments about their mannerisms, and more recently singled out NYT’s Maggie Haberman, calling her “Maggot Hagerman”The timing of the ban appears linked to increasingly critical coverage of the President and his family from sections of the media, including a Bloomberg's review of financial disclosures found that Trump or his money managers made nearly 28,700 securities transactions between his second inauguration and June 30, 2026, more than all members of Congress collectively. Then ProPublica reported that Russian businessman Umar Kremlev, who has ties to the Putin government, financed hundreds of thousands of dollars of expenses surrounding Donald Trump Jr.'s Bahamas wedding celebrations. The U.S media has also become increasingly skeptical of the claims from Trump and his administration on the Iran war, detailing fiascos that the Pentagon has not disclosed.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Denmark confirms US-Greenland security pact, rules out sovereignty transfer
articles.summary: Europe News: Denmark and Greenland on Saturday confirmed that a planned security agreement with the United States will not compromise the sovereignty of the Kingdo.
articles.body: Denmark and Greenland on Saturday confirmed that a planned security agreement with the United States will not compromise the sovereignty of the Kingdom of Denmark or Greenlanders’ right to self-determination. The statement came after US president Donald Trump said the pact would give Washington “permanent control” over the Arctic island’s security.The United States, Denmark and Greenland are expected to sign the agreement on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York next week. It will take effect after the necessary national parliamentary procedures are completed, according to the Danish government.The agreement would allow the United States to develop a significant military presence on Greenland while preventing US adversaries from establishing bases on the island. However, key details, including the scale of the proposed US military presence and whether Washington would receive any formal authority over foreign policy or resources, remain unclear.Greenland prime minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen welcomed the planned accord.“I am pleased on Greenland’s behalf that we are nearing the conclusion of an agreement - an agreement that benefits not only our collective security but also the continued development of this country,” Nielsen said.“The agreement recognizes the sovereignty and territorial integrity of our Kingdom and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination,” he added.Danish prime minister Mette Frederiksen also backed the agreement, saying it would strengthen security in the Arctic and North Atlantic.“I am glad that we are about to make a great agreement for Greenland, the Kingdom of Denmark, and the United States. An agreement which strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic Area and therefore is great for NATO and Europe as well,” Frederiksen said.She stressed that the pact recognises “the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom and the Greenlandic people's right to self-determination.”Denmark’s foreign minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said, “Next week could be a good week - for Greenland, Denmark, and the United States.”“A time of uncertainty will hopefully give way to a binding agreement that strengthens security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic, and thereby our shared security within NATO and Europe - while respecting the (Danish) Kingdom's red lines,” he said.Trump, however, described the arrangement in broader terms, saying, “The United States will FOREVER have the complete ability to do what is necessary in Greenland in order to secure and defend the security of Greenland, and the United States of America.”He said the deal “gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland”, while ruling out bases, military presence or sensitive investments by adversaries without US approval.The agreement follows months of tension after Trump threatened to seize Greenland, straining relations with Denmark and raising concerns within NATO. The alliance said the pact would “help advance security, stability and cooperation in this vital region”.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Danger to India not from communism, but Hindu right-wing communalism': Ansari cites Nehru; BJP hits back
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Former vice president Mohammad Hamid Ansari on Saturday cited former prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru's remarks about the “danger to India” .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former vice president Mohammad Hamid Ansari on Saturday cited former prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru's remarks about the “danger to India” while referring to concerns raised by late constitutional expert and author AG Noorani in his book The RSS: A Menace to India.He was addressing the event, titled “Remembering a Polymath: The Life and Times of Abdul Ghafoor Noorani”, organised at the India Islamic Cultural Centre to commemorate the life and works of the jurist and author.Addressing an event, Ansari recalled jurist and author Abdul Ghafoor Noorani's observations in the introduction to his 2019 book and cited remarks by Nehru that were recorded by former Foreign Secretary Jagat Singh Gundevia during a meeting of Ministry of External Affairs officials.‘The RSS: A Menace to India’ was the title of the book published in 2019. The opening lines of the introduction, where A.G. Noorani used a couplet, reflected what he described as the prevailing sentiment among Muslims in India today. In the same introduction, he referred to former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru’s remarks at a Ministry of External Affairs officers’ meeting, documented by Foreign Secretary Gundevia. Nehru had warned that ‘the real danger to India was not communism, but Hindu right-wing communalism’," he said.During his speech, Ansari discussed Noorani's writings and his views on nationalism, identity and political developments in India. He also referred to Noorani's criticism of what he saw as a shift from civic nationalism towards cultural nationalism.“In recent years, we have experienced the emergence of trends and practices that dispute the well-established principle of civic nationalism and interpose a new and imaginary practice of cultural nationalism,” Ansari said.“It seeks to present an electoral majority in the guise of a religious majority and monopolise political power. It wants to distinguish citizens based on their faith, give vent to intolerance, insinuate otherness, and promote disquiet and insecurity,” he added.Ansari raised concerns over what he described as emerging trends that challenge the principle of civic nationalism.During his speech, Ansari said, “Some of its recent manifestations are chilling and reflect poorly on our claim to be governed by the rule of law. It’s a question that has to be answered. These trends need to be contested and contested legally and contested politically.”'Congress’s anti-Hindu politics in the spotlight', says BJPReacting to Ansari's remarks, the BJP Scheduled Tribe Morcha said the statement brought what it described as Congress's “anti-Hindu politics” into focus. The BJP unit also referred to Rahul Gandhi's past remarks on Hindu groups and terrorism, alleging that such statements reflected a pattern in the party's political narrative."A remark from Nehru that Hamid Ansari highlighted, once again putting Congress’s anti-Hindu politics in the spotlight. Alongside Rahul Gandhi’s past remarks on Hindu groups and terrorism, that such statements reflect a pattern in the party’s political narrative," BJP said in a post on X.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: “He is touching my clothes”: Woman without ticket argues with TTE, tears her own clothes and allegedly threatens him with a case; watch
articles.summary: A video is going viral on social media for all the wrong reasons. It shows a woman arguing with a Travelling Ticket Examiner (TTE) during a train jour.
articles.body: A video is going viral on social media for all the wrong reasons. It shows a woman arguing with a Travelling Ticket Examiner (TTE) during a train journey. The video raises some serious questions. It shows the woman allegedly tearing her own clothes as the TTE confronts her for the ticket. She allegedly starts accusing the railway employee of inappropriate behaviour. The incident, which surfaced on social media on September 18, has since taken the internet by storm.What the viral video showsAs per reports, the incident took place during a ticket inspection on a train. The woman, unable to show a valid ticket when asked by the TTE, starts tearing her clothes. The argument escalated soon with the passenger reportedly making allegations against the railway employee. A video recorded during the confrontation shows the woman tearing parts of her clothing while continuing the argument.However, the exact location or the name of the train remains unclear.The same video continues and identifies herself as Radhika Tiwari. During the argument, she is reportedly heard speaking to a family member over the phone and alleging that the TTE had behaved inappropriately with her. She says, “ye mera kapda choo raha hai yaar”.She then reportedly threatened the TTE that she has a brother who is bigger than him. She also threatens him to call the emergency helpline 112 and accuses him of inappropriate behaviour. And then she starts tearing her clothes, as seen in the video.The TTE appears to have been recording the interaction on his mobile phone. The recording has subsequently circulated widely online.What the woman said when caughtThe woman, when confronted by police officials, allegedly kept denying all the allegations. In the video, a female police officer can be seen asking her why she did what she did. To which the woman says she didn’t do anything and that the TTE was misbehaving with her.Railway Seva’s reaction Railway Seva, the official X account for support to RailUsers, took to X and responded to the video asking for details.“Please share your PNR number and mobile no. preferably via DM to enable us to take immediate action. You may also raise your concern directly on RailMadad or dial 139 for speedy redressal,” Railway Seva said.What happens when a passenger has no ticket?Under the Railways Act, those travelling without a valid ticket can attract the applicable fare along with an excess charge and fine. The legal framework was amended in 2026 under the Jan Vishwas reforms. The minimum excess charge for relevant ticketless or irregular travel cases was raised from ₹250 to ₹500.The amended provisions cover situations including travelling without proper authorisation and certain cases of travelling beyond the distance permitted by a ticket. If a passenger refuses or fails to pay the amount demanded under the applicable provisions, the railway authorities can pursue recovery through the competent court.Meanwhile, the viral incident raises two separate concerns: The importance of following railway ticketing rules and the need for allegations arising during passenger-staff disputes to be examined through proper channels.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.body: NEW DELHI: ABVP’s Yash Dabas was elected president of the Delhi University Students’ Union (DUSU), while independent candidate Deepanshu Shokeen won the vice-president’s post as results for the four central panel positions were announced on Saturday.Dabas secured 24,576 votes to defeat NSUI’s Vijay Shankar Meena, who polled 22,523 votes. articles.title: Meet Ethan Huynh, the 17-year-old Florida cancer survivor who returned to competitive swimming and raised $45,000 for children fighting cancer through two meets
articles.summary: US News: A teenager who once struggled to get out of bed during cancer treatment is now back in the pool, using the sport he loves to help children facing the .
articles.body: A teenager who once struggled to get out of bed during cancer treatment is now back in the pool, using the sport he loves to help children facing the same disease. Ethan Huynh, a 17-year-old student at Montverde Academy near Orlando, Florida, survived brain cancer after being diagnosed in 2023. He later returned to competitive swimming and turned his races into fundraising opportunities. At two Orlando swim meets, his efforts raised a combined $45,000 for cancer-related causes, according to WESH 2, a Central Florida NBC-affiliated news station that detailed Ethan's cancer journey, his return to swimming and his efforts to support other children fighting cancer.Ethan's cancer diagnosis changed his lifeEthan's journey began in 2023, when severe headaches led to his brain cancer diagnosis. The sudden change was difficult for the teenager and his family, particularly because they had already experienced cancer treatment through another member of the family. Just over a year before Ethan's diagnosis, his younger brother Christian had completed treatment for leukemia. That meant the family was already familiar with the emotional and physical demands of childhood cancer when Ethan began his own treatment.Speaking to WESH 2, Ethan recalled how quickly his life changed after his diagnosis. He also described the effects of chemotherapy, including periods when he had little appetite and became so weak that he could not get out of bed. His mother, Lien Van, told WESH 2 that having two children go through cancer treatment felt almost impossible statistically, while both ultimately surviving and continuing to thrive.Swimming became part of his recoveryBefore cancer interrupted his life, swimming was an important part of Ethan's routine. After completing treatment, he gradually returned to the sport. His return was more than simply getting back into competition. Swimming became a way for Ethan to transform his experience as a cancer survivor into an opportunity to help other children. Rather than keeping his fundraising separate from his athletic activities, he connected the two. His participation in swim meets became a way of drawing attention to childhood cancer while collecting donations for organisations involved in cancer research and support.Ethan's experience also gave him a personal reason to focus on other young people going through treatment. Having experienced chemotherapy himself, he understood the physical demands and uncertainty that can accompany a cancer diagnosis.Two swim meets raised $45,000In May 2026, Ethan competed in the Golden Mile Swim Meet in Orlando, where his fundraising efforts generated $32,000 for St. Jude Children's Research Hospital. He later participated in another Orlando swimming event organised with Swim Across America. His swimming at that meet raised an additional $13,000. Together, the two efforts brought the total to $45,000.The fundraising demonstrated how Ethan was able to use his return to competitive swimming as a platform for supporting children and families affected by cancer. His efforts were not based simply on raising money; they were also connected to his own experience of surviving treatment.An experience that created a personal promiseFor Ethan, giving back became something he felt compelled to do after completing treatment. Speaking to WESH 2, he said that surviving treatment and continuing to thrive afterward left him feeling that he had an internal promise to fulfil. That motivation has shaped his approach to swimming and fundraising. Instead of viewing his recovery as the end of his cancer story, Ethan has used it as a starting point for supporting other children. His work has also earned him recognition as a community champion.A message for children fighting cancerEthan's story has also given him a chance to speak directly to other young people going through cancer treatment. Ethan encouraged children facing cancer to continue fighting even when the battle initially seems difficult. He also emphasised the importance of having people around them for support, according to WESH 2. His message reflects his own experience, from the difficult period of treatment to returning to a sport he loved and finding a way to help others.For Ethan, the swimming pool has therefore become more than a place to compete. It has become a place where his recovery, athletic ambitions and desire to support other children have come together.Turning survival into supportEthan's $45,000 fundraising total came from two separate swimming events, but the significance of the effort goes beyond the amount raised. His journey shows how a teenager who went through his own cancer treatment has returned to an activity that was important to him and used it to support children facing similar challenges. His younger brother's leukemia journey, followed by Ethan's own brain cancer diagnosis, gave the family two deeply personal experiences with childhood cancer. Ethan's decision to return to swimming and raise money for cancer causes has now added another chapter to that story.At 17, he is continuing to compete, raise awareness and encourage other young cancer patients to keep moving forward with support from the people around them.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: US glider planes collide mid-air in New York, one pilot killed
articles.summary: US News: A glider pilot was killed after two glider planes collided midair over Saratoga County in New York on Friday, authorities said.According to the New Yo.
articles.body: A glider pilot was killed after two glider planes collided midair over Saratoga County in New York on Friday, authorities said.According to the New York State Police, the collision took place near Wheeler Road in the town of Edinburg shortly before 2:30 pm. Police, forest rangers, and the Saratoga County Sheriff's Office launched a search, and the wreckage of one glider was later found in a remote area near Sand Lake Road.The pilot of the crashed glider was found dead at the scene. Authorities have not yet released the pilot’s identity.The second glider managed to land safely at Plateau Sky Ranch Airport, and its pilot was not injured, police said. Neither aircraft had any passengers on board.The Federal Aviation Administration identified the crashed aircraft as a Schempp-Hirth Ventus, while the glider that landed safely was a Schleicher AS24.The crash triggered a major response from local emergency services. The National Transportation Safety Board will lead the investigation into the collision, the FAA said.Edinburg, a town of more than 1,300 people, is located about 54 miles northwest of Albany.In another incident that took place on Tuesday, at least three people were killed after a helicopter being used by NBC News crashed into a parking lot in Los Angeles, officials said.The helicopter went down shortly before 7 pm near a storage facility in Chatsworth, a neighborhood in Los Angeles’ San Fernando Valley, according to officials.NBC4 Los Angeles anchor Colleen Williams confirmed the crash during a live broadcast before the station abruptly cut its coverage.“We’re going to take a couple of minutes to process this,” Williams said, her voice shaking.The helicopter crash occurred as news crews were covering a separate bus crash in the area. The bus crash killed at least two people and injured six others, according to the Los Angeles Fire Department.The circumstances surrounding the helicopter crash were not immediately clear.
